video_title: Micha Nori Postgame Interview | Portland Trail Blazers 116, GS Warriors 94 | Nov. 27, 2026

quotes.speaker: Micha Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micha Nori on the team's competitive spirit and roster depth
quotes.excerpt: anytime you put yourself in an opportunity to win something, and say what you want, with a very tough group.
quotes.quote: I'm happy for the guys. I'm happy for my staff. Anytime you put yourself in an opportunity to win something, and say what you want, with a very tough group. When you talk about the Lakers, the Spurs, you talk about ourselves, and then obviously Sacramento and Golden State. God bless them, they've had some injuries, but they were playing just as well as anybody before the injury bug got them as well. It was happy for our guys. I think we have Memphis, I don't know the date, but that's what it sounds like.
quotes.social_post: Micha Nori on the Blazers competitive spirit after the win against Golden State: I am happy for the guys and my staff. Anytime you put yourself in an opportunity to win something you have to be proud of this tough group.

structured.context: Micha Nori discusses the team's competitive standing in the Western Conference and mentions injuries affecting other teams.

quotes.speaker: Micha Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micha Nori on the decision to keep starters in late
quotes.excerpt: I asked Jacob what the score was going on with the Spurs, and that's when we found out.
quotes.quote: I knew what we needed at the start, and who we needed to win, and then it became we knew what the number was. I asked Jacob what the score was going on with the Spurs, and that's when we found out it was like a two-possession game with 40 seconds, so that's why we left the guys in. The whole thing gets you a little discombobulated, you're worried about this, what the score here, this, the other thing, and the other. So we were a little discombobulated in that regard, but it was good.
quotes.social_post: Micha Nori explains why he kept his starters in late during the win: I asked Jacob what the score was with the Spurs and when we found out it was a two possession game we left the guys in. The whole thing gets you a little discombobulated.

structured.context: Micha Nori explains why he kept his starters in the game late based on the score of the Spurs game.

quotes.speaker: Micha Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micha Nori on the team's perception as a 'feel-good story'
quotes.excerpt: I've never thought of us as a feel-good story. We have a really good roster with really good players.
quotes.quote: I don't mean to sound like this, but no disrespect to anybody, I don't really care what people think as far as if we're a good story this or that. I think that I'm happy because the Blazers as an organization and those players, these fans and all that, I think it's great for what's going on here for the excitement that it builds around the city. But I've never thought of us as a feel-good story. We have a really good roster with really good players, and we are in a tough Western Conference.
quotes.social_post: Micha Nori pushes back on the Blazers being a feel good story: I do not really care what people think. I have never thought of us as a feel good story. We have a really good roster with really good players in a tough Western Conference.

structured.context: Micha Nori reacts to the media narrative surrounding the team's success this season.

quotes.speaker: Micha Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micha Nori provides an update on Hounson's ankle injury
quotes.excerpt: He sprained his ankle playing five-on-five today, just in kind of our guys that we want to make sure.
quotes.quote: He sprained his ankle playing five-on-five today, just in kind of our guys that we want to make sure they stay sharp and get some extra minutes. So he just happened to come down on a guy's foot. I think that they'll look at it tomorrow, just get it settled down, and just precautionary right now. I don't know, I don't think it's, I don't know how bad it is. I don't want to comment on because I don't know, because it just happened at the end of shootaround.
quotes.social_post: Micha Nori provides an injury update on Hounson: He sprained his ankle playing five on five today. They will look at it tomorrow to get it settled down. It is just precautionary right now.

structured.context: Micha Nori provides an update on Hounson, who sprained his ankle during a practice session.

quotes.speaker: Micha Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micha Nori on Hounson's role after returning from injury
quotes.excerpt: When Rob's been out, or we've needed, and we've had some foul trouble, he's right there as that third center.
quotes.quote: I foresee Hounson's role staying the same. When Rob's been out, or we've needed, and we've had some foul trouble, he's right there as that third center, and I think the minutes that Hounson has has gotten has served him well, and that's where he'll stay for the time being.
quotes.social_post: Micha Nori on Hounson's role moving forward: I foresee Hounson's role staying the same. He is right there as that third center and the minutes he has gotten have served him well so that is where he will stay for the time being.

structured.context: Micha Nori clarifies that Hounson's role in the rotation will remain unchanged despite recent injury concerns.

quotes.speaker: Micha Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micha Nori on the impact of the loss to Memphis
quotes.excerpt: Does that give you guys any extra juice to I know they're not they don't have Boozer right now.
quotes.quote: Yeah, I think so. Again, I think that we kind of felt that way with San Antonio. San Antonio came in here and quite honestly embarrassed us, and sent Minnesota, the team I was with, and Portland, we've talked about that home. And then to come in here and I think we were maybe three and 0, right? Coming back home and they were obviously, and they beat us pretty soundly too. I think we'll go look at the tape. I mean, I think that they're a very physical team, obviously. They're much a little bit like us, pretty deep team. And that game was one of those ones as well where we had some good looks, we couldn't make a shot. I think Boozer, God blessing, probably going to be rookie of the year if he stays healthy, but I think he made every single one of his threes that he's made this season dag on near against us.
quotes.social_post: Micha Nori on facing Memphis: They are a very physical team and pretty deep. I think Boozer is probably going to be rookie of the year if he stays healthy. He made every single one of his threes against us.

structured.context: Micha Nori reflects on past losses and praises the performance of Boozer.

quotes.speaker: Micha Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micha Nori on the team's defensive focus in big games
quotes.excerpt: The one way that we can get a point differential is if we just play defense every single possession.
quotes.quote: We knew we had to win by a big amount. Large amount, excuse me. And you can't say score more points because it's like you can't like, you know, because then guys are sitting there they get like trying to, you know, force shots or every they're living and dying with every shot. And I challenged the group and just said, hey, the one way that we can get a point differential is if we just play defense every single possession as if it's a last possession of a basketball game. And they came out and, you know, 37 to 11. Maybe I should have said it again at the end of the first quarter.
quotes.social_post: Micha Nori on the defensive focus needed for point differential: I challenged the group to play defense every single possession as if it is the last possession of a basketball game. They came out and held them to 11 points in the first.

structured.context: Micha Nori explains his defensive challenge to the team to improve their point differential.

quotes.speaker: Micha Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micha Nori on Michael Potter's performance and development
quotes.excerpt: Tonight it was really Michael Potter who shined, you know, 11 points in 12 minutes.
quotes.quote: Tonight it was really Michael Potter who shined, you know, 11 points in 12 minutes. And Brandon Carlson has kind of been that that next guy, and Michael went in ahead of him tonight. And I don't know why, but for whatever reason, I just had and driving down here trying to think about who we could, and I just kept flashing back to that preseason game when Michael Potter basically turned the I know it's preseason, I know it doesn't matter, but we're playing Golden State. He gets the steal, he hits a big three, and it's just sometimes you get a hunch, sometimes you just, you know, you throw it out there and see what happens, and I thought that he responded great.
quotes.social_post: Micha Nori on Michael Potter's 11 points in 12 minutes: Sometimes you get a hunch and you just throw it out there and see what happens. I thought he responded great.

structured.context: Micha Nori explains his decision to play Michael Potter over Brandon Carlson based on a hunch.
